class ReexpandTests(ReexpandTestBase):
    def test_reexpand_after_delete_replaces_every_record_and_queues_from_zero(self):
        self.expand(items=(1, 2, 3))
        self.complete("run-1", "a2", {"v": 0})
        self.service.delete_map_instance("run-1", "fanout", 1, {}, "d1")
        state = self.service.expand_map("run-1", "fanout", {}, "x1")
        instances = state["maps"]["fanout"]["instances"]
        self.assertEqual([0, 1, 2], [item["index"] for item in instances])
        self.assertTrue(all(item["status"] == "ready" for item in instances))
        self.assertEqual("running", state["maps"]["fanout"]["status"])
        # The completed instance's old output is gone with its record.
        self.assertTrue(all(item["output"] is None for item in instances))
        # The fresh instances advance one per call, in index order.
        self.complete("run-1", "a3", {"v": 10})
        self.complete("run-1", "a4", {"v": 11})
        state = self.complete("run-1", "a5", {"v": 12})
        self.assertEqual("completed", state["maps"]["fanout"]["status"])
        # The result list holds only the finally retained instances' outputs.
        self.assertEqual([{"v": 10}, {"v": 11}, {"v": 12}], state["outputs"]["fanout"])
        self.assertTrue(self.service.replay("run-1")["consistent"])

    def test_reexpand_event_matches_first_expansion_shape(self):
        self.expand(items=(1, 2))
        self.service.delete_map_instance("run-1", "fanout", 0, {}, "d1")
        self.service.expand_map("run-1", "fanout", {}, "x1")
        expanded = [event for event in self.service.events("run-1") if event["type"] == "map_expanded"]
        self.assertEqual(2, len(expanded))
        self.assertEqual(
            {"map_id": "fanout", "instance_count": 2, "exceeded": False}, expanded[-1]["payload"]
        )
        self.assertNotIn("loop_id", expanded[-1]["payload"])

    def test_reexpanded_instances_retry_and_delete_like_first_expansion(self):
        self.expand(workflow({"id": "work", "retries": 1}), items=(1, 2))
        # Burn the retry budget of instance 0 before re-expanding.
        self.service.advance("run-1", {"failure": {"reason": "boom"}}, "a2")
        self.service.expand_map("run-1", "fanout", {}, "x1")
        # The fresh instance 0 has a fresh budget: its first failure retries.
        state = self.service.advance("run-1", {"failure": {"reason": "boom"}}, "a3")
        self.assertEqual("ready", state["maps"]["fanout"]["instances"][0]["status"])
        self.assertEqual("running", state["status"])
        # Delete and modify entries apply to the new list exactly as before.
        self.service.modify_map_instance("run-1", "fanout", 1, {"input": {"k": 1}}, "m1")
        state = self.service.delete_map_instance("run-1", "fanout", 1, {}, "d1")
        self.assertEqual([0], [item["index"] for item in state["maps"]["fanout"]["instances"]])
        state = self.complete("run-1", "a4", {"v": 0})
        self.assertEqual([{"v": 0}], state["outputs"]["fanout"])
        self.assertTrue(self.service.replay("run-1")["consistent"])

    def test_reexpanded_instances_park_for_approval_like_first_expansion(self):
        self.expand(workflow({"id": "work", "approval": {"approvers": ["alice"]}}), items=(1,))
        self.service.delete_map_instance("run-1", "fanout", 0, {}, "d1")
        # Deleting the only instance completed the node, so this map is done.
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            self.service.expand_map("run-1", "fanout", {}, "x1")

    def test_pending_completed_or_failed_map_cannot_reexpand(self):
        # Pending: the map never expanded (its source has not completed).
        self.service.create_workflow(workflow(), "w1")
        self.service.create_execution({"id": "run-p", "workflow_id": "orders", "input": {}}, "e-p")
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            self.service.expand_map("run-p", "fanout", {}, "x-p")
        # Completed: every retained instance finished.
        self.expand(items=(1,))
        self.complete("run-1", "a2", {"v": 0})
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            self.service.expand_map("run-1", "fanout", {}, "x-c")
        # Failed: retry exhaustion terminated the execution.
        self.expand(workflow({"id": "work", "retries": 0}), execution_id="run-2", items=(1,))
        self.service.advance("run-2", {"failure": {"reason": "boom"}}, "a-f")
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            self.service.expand_map("run-2", "fanout", {}, "x-f")

    def test_unknown_targets_are_not_found(self):
        self.expand(items=(1,))
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            self.service.expand_map("run-1", "ghost", {}, "x1")
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            self.service.expand_map("missing", "fanout", {}, "x2")
        # A node that is not a dynamic map is not found either.
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            self.service.expand_map("run-1", "collect", {}, "x3")

    def test_non_empty_body_is_a_validation_error(self):

        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.service.expand_map("run-1", "fanout", [], "x2")

    def test_expand_is_idempotent_and_scoped_per_operation(self):

        self.service.delete_map_instance("run-1", "fanout", 0, {}, "d1")
        first = self.service.expand_map("run-1", "fanout", {}, "shared")
        second = self.service.expand_map("run-1", "fanout", {}, "shared")
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        expanded = [event for event in self.service.events("run-1") if event["type"] == "map_expanded"]
        self.assertEqual(2, len(expanded))
        # The same key names another operation everywhere else.

        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            self.service.modify_map_instance("run-1", "fanout", 1, {"input": {}}, "shared")

        self.expand(items=(1,), tenant="acme")

    def test_modify_then_delete_settles_in_call_order(self):

        self.service.modify_map_instance("run-1", "fanout", 0, {"input": {"k": 1}}, "m1")

        self.assertEqual([1], [item["index"] for item in state["maps"]["fanout"]["instances"]])

        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        cls.server.shutdown()
        cls.server.server_close()
        cls.directory.cleanup()

    @classmethod
    def call(cls, method, path, body=None, key=None):
        connection = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", cls.port)
        headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
        if key is not None:
            headers["Idempotency-Key"] = key
        connection.request(method, path, json.dumps(body) if body is not None else None, headers)
        response = connection.getresponse()
        data = response.read()
        connection.close()
        return response.status, data

    def test_expand_round_trip_over_http(self):
        status, data = self.call("POST", "/executions/run-1/maps/fanout/instances/0/delete", {}, "hd1")
        self.assertEqual(200, status)

        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertTrue(data.endswith(b"\n"))
        self.assertFalse(data.endswith(b"\n\n"))
        body = json.loads(data)
        self.assertEqual([0, 1], [item["index"] for item in body["maps"]["fanout"]["instances"]])
        self.assertTrue(all(item["status"] == "ready" for item in body["maps"]["fanout"]["instances"]))

    def test_expand_body_and_target_errors_over_http(self):
        status, data = self.call("POST", "/executions/run-1/maps/fanout/expand", {"x": 1}, "hx2")
        self.assertEqual(400, status)

        self.assertEqual(404, status)

### Delete and modify expanded instances

An expanded dynamic node offers, alongside expansion and per-instance
advancement, two instance-level operations. Both are ordinary idempotent
HTTP commands over the same entry points the rest of the service uses; they
introduce no second protocol.

An instance that has never advanced can be removed, and so can an instance
that has permanently failed:

```http
POST /executions/run-1/maps/ship/instances/2/delete
Idempotency-Key: delete-instance-2

{}
```

content.content:
- an `instance_deleted` event records the action type, the owning dynamic
  node under `map_id`, the removed instance's element `index` and `status`
  (`ready` or `failed`), and, for a map inside a loop body, the `loop_id`
  and `iteration`;
- an `instance_modified` event records the action type, the owning
  `map_id`, the instance `index`, the content `before` the rewrite (`null`
  for an instance that had never been rewritten) and `after` it, and the
  same loop context when the instance belongs to an iteration.

Replay rebuilds the instance list, every instance's status and ownership,
and each rewrite solely from the event stream: a delete drops the recorded
instance (and the subsequent `map_completed`, when the deletion finished the
node, completes it with the retained outputs), and a modify applies the
rewritten input to that one instance, so the rebuilt state is exactly the
materialized state. A checkpoint is written at the instance boundary of
every successful delete or modify; after a restart recovery continues the
unfinished instances, repeats no instance output, and never resurrects a
deleted instance. The operations change no advancement conclusion or
termination semantics: cancellation, timeouts, approvals, leases, retries,
and retry exhaustion keep their existing behavior. Executions that never
use either operation keep exactly their current state fields, event
contents, and advancement results. Interleaving a deletion and a
modification on the same instance, re-expanding a map after a deletion, and
modifying a node that is not a dynamic map are out of scope.

}

1	# ChronicleFlow
2	
3	ChronicleFlow is a small backend for durable workflow orchestration. It stores
4	workflow definitions, execution state, and an append-only event history in
5	SQLite so an execution can be inspected and replayed deterministically.
6	
7	The initial release intentionally supports a compact public contract:
8	
9	- workflows are directed acyclic graphs of `task`, `condition`, bounded
10	  `loop`, and dynamic `map` nodes;
11	- a workflow may declare named versions: every declared version is kept and
12	  each execution is bound to the version that was current (or explicitly
13	  named) when it started, so upgrading a workflow never changes a running
14	  execution, and a running execution can be explicitly migrated to another
15	  version of the same workflow, after which it advances under that version;
16	- executions advance one ready task at a time, evaluating conditions and
17	  skipping unmatched branches automatically;
18	- task nodes may declare a bounded number of retries: a submitted failure
19	  re-queues the node until the retries are exhausted, which terminates the
20	  execution;
21	- a task node may declare an approval point with the people allowed to decide
22	  it; advancing parks the task in a waiting state until an approver approves
23	  (completing it with the submitted output) or rejects (terminating the
24	  execution with reason `rejected`);
25	- executions may declare a timeout in seconds, after which they terminate and
26	  no longer accept output, and they may be cancelled explicitly;
27	- loop nodes repeat their body a bounded number of times, re-evaluating a
28	  continue condition at the loop boundaries;
29	- a map node inside a loop body expands independently in every iteration
30	  from that iteration's source output, its instances and events belonging
31	  to the iteration they expanded in;
32	- every state transition is appended to the execution event stream;
33	- replay rebuilds execution state from the recorded events;
34	- a checkpoint is written at every node boundary, capturing the state
35	  summary and event position, so an execution can be recovered from the
36	  latest checkpoint after a restart;
37	- workers may claim a running execution to receive a work item with a
38	  time-bounded lease, renew the lease with heartbeats, and release it;
39	  while a lease is active only its holder may submit results, and an
40	  expired or released lease returns the work item to the claimable set;
41	- duplicate commands with the same idempotency key return the original result;
42	- workflows and executions may declare webhook subscriptions, and matching
43	  business events are delivered to the declared targets with bounded retries,
44	  each delivery recorded in a per-execution history;
45	- subscriptions may also declare queue targets instead of webhook addresses:
46	  matching business events are appended, in occurrence order, to persistent
47	  per-execution queues that callers pull from and acknowledge explicitly,
48	  with a visibility timeout returning unacknowledged messages to the pending
49	  set (delivery is at least once);
50	- a workflow may declare a schedule — a fixed interval in seconds or a
51	  five-field cron plan — and the service automatically creates one execution
52	  per due period with the declared input; schedules can be paused and
53	  resumed, and periods missed while paused are either caught up once or
54	  skipped, according to the declared missed policy.
55	
56	## Requirements
57	
58	- Python 3.11 or newer
59	- no third-party runtime dependencies
60	
61	## Run the service
62	
63	```bash
64	PYTHONPATH=src python -m chronicleflow.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --database chronicleflow.db
65	```
66	
67	The process prints `ChronicleFlow listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080` after it
68	has bound the port.
69	
70	## HTTP API
71	
72	All request and response bodies are JSON. Unknown fields are rejected.
73	
74	Responses are compact JSON with no insignificant whitespace, and every
75	response body ends with exactly one trailing newline (`\n`). Numbers
76	round-trip with their full precision: finite floats keep their original
77	IEEE-754 value through the shortest textual representation that decodes to
78	it (so `0.30000000000000004` stays `0.30000000000000004`), negative zero is
79	preserved as `-0.0`, and integers stay integers. Non-finite numbers may
80	never appear in a request and are never produced in a response; timestamps
81	are ISO-8601 UTC strings ending in `Z`.
82	
83	### Tenants and quotas
84	
85	A request may declare a tenant by sending the `X-Tenant-Id` header with a
86	non-empty identifier. Every workflow, execution, schedule, schedule status,
87	delivery history, and queue record is scoped to the tenant of the request that
88	created it: queries and operations only ever see data belonging to that
89	tenant, and different tenants may use the same workflow or execution
90	identifiers without colliding. Referencing another tenant's resource — for
91	example advancing, migrating, deciding, claiming, cancelling, recovering, replaying, or
92	reading the events, checkpoints, deliveries, queues, or schedule of an execution or
93	workflow owned by another tenant, or pulling from or acknowledging one of its
94	queues — is answered exactly like a reference to a
95	missing resource: `404 not_found`, with no indication that the resource
96	exists elsewhere. An execution created in one tenant can only reference a
97	workflow of the same tenant, and a migration can only name a version of that
98	workflow in the same tenant; referencing an unseen workflow identifier or
99	version is the usual `404 not_found`.
100	
101	The header applies to every workflow, execution, and schedule entry point,
102	including creation, advancement, migration, approval decisions, lease
103	operations, cancellation, recovery, replay, instance deletion and
104	modification, queue pulls, acknowledgements, and all history and status
105	queries, as well as the usage, bill, and metrics queries. An empty
106	`X-Tenant-Id` value is a `400 validation_error`. Requests that omit the
107	header entirely keep using the single legacy namespace, whose advancement,
108	approvals, leases, retries, timeouts, cancellation, checkpoints, recovery,
109	scheduling, and replay behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged: the tenant is
110	stored only as database scope, never added to a state field or event payload,
111	and state shapes and event streams gain no new fields. Idempotency keys are
112	scoped per tenant as well, so tenants can never see or collide with each
113	other's keys; reusing a key for another operation within the same tenant is
114	the usual `409 conflict`.
115	
116	A tenant may declare quotas bounding how many workflows and executions it may

122	X-Tenant-Id: acme

2	
3	ChronicleFlow is a small backend for durable workflow orchestration. It stores
4	workflow definitions, execution state, and an append-only event history in
5	SQLite so an execution can be inspected and replayed deterministically.
6	
7	The initial release intentionally supports a compact public contract:
8	
9	- workflows are directed acyclic graphs of `task`, `condition`, bounded
10	  `loop`, and dynamic `map` nodes;
11	- a workflow may declare named versions: every declared version is kept and
12	  each execution is bound to the version that was current (or explicitly
13	  named) when it started, so upgrading a workflow never changes a running
14	  execution, and a running execution can be explicitly migrated to another
15	  version of the same workflow, after which it advances under that version;
16	- executions advance one ready task at a time, evaluating conditions and
17	  skipping unmatched branches automatically;
18	- task nodes may declare a bounded number of retries: a submitted failure
19	  re-queues the node until the retries are exhausted, which terminates the
20	  execution;
21	- a task node may declare an approval point with the people allowed to decide
22	  it; advancing parks the task in a waiting state until an approver approves
23	  (completing it with the submitted output) or rejects (terminating the
24	  execution with reason `rejected`);
25	- executions may declare a timeout in seconds, after which they terminate and
26	  no longer accept output, and they may be cancelled explicitly;
27	- loop nodes repeat their body a bounded number of times, re-evaluating a
28	  continue condition at the loop boundaries;
29	- a map node inside a loop body expands independently in every iteration
30	  from that iteration's source output, its instances and events belonging
31	  to the iteration they expanded in;
32	- every state transition is appended to the execution event stream;
33	- replay rebuilds execution state from the recorded events;
34	- a checkpoint is written at every node boundary, capturing the state
35	  summary and event position, so an execution can be recovered from the
36	  latest checkpoint after a restart;
37	- workers may claim a running execution to receive a work item with a
38	  time-bounded lease, renew the lease with heartbeats, and release it;
39	  while a lease is active only its holder may submit results, and an
40	  expired or released lease returns the work item to the claimable set;
41	- duplicate commands with the same idempotency key return the original result;
42	- workflows and executions may declare webhook subscriptions, and matching
43	  business events are delivered to the declared targets with bounded retries,
44	  each delivery recorded in a per-execution history;

### Delete, modify, and re-expand expanded instances

An expanded dynamic node offers, alongside expansion and per-instance
advancement, two instance-level operations and one node-level re-expansion.
All are ordinary idempotent HTTP commands over the same entry points the
rest of the service uses; they introduce no second protocol.

An instance that has never advanced can be removed, and so can an instance
that has permanently failed:

```http
POST /executions/run-1/maps/ship/instances/2/delete
Idempotency-Key: delete-instance-2

{}
```

The body must be an empty object. Removing an instance drops only that
instance's record: every retained instance keeps its element index, its
place in the queue, and its advancement order. When the removed instance was
the map's last unfinished instance, the node completes under the existing
rules with an output list containing only the retained instances' outputs,
in ascending element-index order, and its successors unlock as usual. An
instance that is waiting on an approval, or has already completed, can never
be deleted; attempting it returns `409 conflict` and changes no state. A
permanently failed instance is removable after the execution has terminated,
but removing it never revives the execution, alters its termination reason,
or changes the node's failed conclusion. When every retained instance of a
map inside a loop body has ended, the iteration's other nodes advance as
usual and the node completes or ends under the existing rules; deleting an
instance in one iteration never touches another iteration.

An instance that has never advanced can also have its input rewritten
before it is worked:

```http
POST /executions/run-1/maps/ship/instances/1/modify
Idempotency-Key: modify-instance-1

{"input":{"address":"742 Evergreen Terrace"}}
```

The body must contain exactly `input`, an object with the new content; it is
validated like every other request body (finite numbers only). The rewrite
changes only the parameters used when that one instance is later advanced:
it affects no other instance, and the output and history of an instance that
